title: “My Grace Is Sufficient”… But Why Does It Still Hurt?
paragraphs:
“My Grace Is Sufficient”… But Why Does It Still Hurt?
The Verse We Love to Quote, the Truth We Often Avoid, and the Scandalous Grace That Changes Everything
There are verses we frame on our walls.
Verses we print on coffee mugs.
Verses we whisper to ourselves when life becomes too heavy.
Among them, few are quoted more often than these words from the Apostle Paul:
"My grace is sufficient for you, for My power is made perfect in weakness." (2 Corinthians 12:9)
But somewhere along the way, many believers unknowingly turned this promise into something Jesus never intended.
We began treating grace as God's guarantee that life would become easier.
We began believing that if we truly trusted Christ, suffering would eventually disappear.
Then the anxiety that refused to leave.
And suddenly the verse we once loved seemed almost impossible to believe.
"If Your grace is sufficient, Lord... why am I still crying?"
It is one of the oldest cries in Scripture.
The Apostle Paul himself asked something remarkably similar.
To understand God's answer, we have to leave behind our modern assumptions and enter the world of the New Testament itself.
Paul writes in 2 Corinthians 12 that he was given what he calls a "thorn in the flesh."
The word σκόλοψ (skólops) was not describing a tiny inconvenience.
It referred to a sharpened stake, a painful splinter, or even something capable of torture.
"Three times I pleaded with the Lord about this, that it should leave me." (2 Corinthians 12:8)
This wasn't a man lacking faith.
This was one of the greatest apostles who ever lived...
Many of us have been taught that persistent suffering must mean weak faith.
But not the answer Paul wanted.
It does not merely mean "barely enough."
"I'll give you just enough to survive."
"My grace lacks absolutely nothing you need."
God did not promise immediate removal of the suffering.
Grace was never primarily about escaping pain.
Grace is God's sustaining presence when pain refuses to leave.
The Hebrew Scriptures prepare us for this long before Paul ever wrote these words.
One of the richest Hebrew words for God's steadfast love is:
No single English word fully captures it.
God's covenant love does not promise a painless life.
It promises that He will never stop being faithful.
Even when circumstances seem to suggest otherwise.
Perhaps nowhere is this clearer than in Isaiah 43.
"When you pass through the waters, I will be with you... when you walk through fire you shall not be burned."
He never promises there will be no waters.
Christianity has never been the promise of an easier road.
It is the promise of Emmanuel.
Even Jesus Himself demonstrates this truth.
"My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from Me."
It was precisely through suffering that redemption entered history.
"For My power is made perfect in weakness."
ἡ γὰρ δύναμίς μου ἐν ἀσθενείᾳ τελεῖται
(hē gar dynamis mou en astheneia teleitai).
God's power reaches its intended goal precisely where human strength reaches its limit.
That overturns everything our culture teaches.
Jesus transforms weakness into a stage where His glory shines brightest.
That is why Paul makes one of the most shocking statements in Scripture:
"Therefore I will boast all the more gladly of my weaknesses."
Only someone who has discovered that weakness is no longer a liability.
It has become the meeting place of divine strength.
The Bible never tells us pain is good.
Disease is still part of a fallen world.
Jesus Himself wept at Lazarus' tomb even though He knew resurrection was moments away.
Some of you reading this have prayed for healing for years.
Some have watched loved ones walk away from Christ.
Some silently battle depression while smiling every Sunday.
Some wonder whether God has forgotten your address.
Hear the words of Jesus again.
Not because your burden is small.
But because Christ is infinitely greater than the burden.
The greatest misunderstanding of grace is believing it exists to make life comfortable.
The greatest revelation of grace is discovering Christ is enough when comfort disappears.
It cost the Son of God everything.
At Golgotha, the world witnessed what appeared to be the greatest scandal imaginable.
The sinless Son of God hanging between criminals.
It looked like God had abandoned His own Messiah.
Yet that very scandal became the doorway to grace.
The resurrection declared what heaven had known all along.
He rewrites Peter's denial into restoration.
He rewrites Paul's persecution into apostleship.
He rewrites the thief's final hours into paradise.
He rewrites your shame into testimony.
That is why our theme has never been a slogan.
It is the heartbeat of the Gospel.
If today's article strengthened your faith, don't let it stop with you.
One day you will discover that the very place where you begged God to remove the thorn became the place where you knew Jesus more deeply than you ever thought possible.
